hints: Let dp[i] be the cheapest cost when the last killed monster is i.
Every earlier choice contributes a line f[j]*s[i]+dp[j].
Insert the initial factor as a line and query a lower hull at each strength.
analogy: Every previously earned skill factor offers a price line; choose the cheapest line for the next monster.
example: With initial factor 10, strengths [2,3], and new factors [1,1], killing both costs 20+3=23 versus 30 for only the last.
algorithm: Start a minimum line hull with y=x_initial*t. For each level i in order, query the minimum at t=s[i] to obtain dp[i], then insert y=f[i]*t+dp[i]. The monotone strengths and factors allow a deque convex hull, handling equal slopes by keeping the smaller intercept. Print dp[n]. Use wide arithmetic.
correctness: If i is killed, the preceding killed monster j or the initial state completely determines its current factor. The recurrence checks all such j, and each hull line represents exactly one valid preceding state.
complexity: For n levels, O(n) time and O(n) space with monotone hull operations.
